name: Mould-baked leavened bread at Old Kingdom Giza
summary: State bakeries at Old Kingdom Giza baked bread in large ceramic moulds to feed the pyramid workforce; the excavators infer from the mould volume that it was leavened.
description: Two bakeries excavated in 1991 in the 4th Dynasty workers' town at Giza (Heit el-Ghurab) held mixing vats, hearths and large bell-shaped ceramic bedja moulds, matching bread-baking scenes in Old Kingdom tombs. The excavators, Ancient Egypt Research Associates, argue from the volume of the moulds that the emmer and barley bread baked in them must have been leavened. This is an inference from the moulds, not a finding of yeast or sourdough residue.

impact.note: Mould-baked bread was the staple ration across Egypt for centuries (reach 2; wider descent to Greek and Roman bread is not sourced), it improved an existing food rather than adding a capability (depth 1), and a few later baking practices followed (generativity 1).

date.label: Old Kingdom (2575-2134 BC)
date.basis: As the cited source gives it.

events.statement: Two bakeries excavated at Giza match the bakeries shown in scenes and models from tombs of the Old Kingdom, which the source dates 2575-2134 BC.

evidence.supports: These bakeries are the archaeological counterparts of the bakeries depicted in many scenes and limestone models from Old Kingdom (2575-2134 BC) tombs.

date.label: 4th Dynasty, Old Kingdom
date.basis: As the cited source gives it.

events.statement: The settlement at Giza in which the bakeries stood dates to the 4th Dynasty; this source gives no years, so the bounds are the Old Kingdom span given by the other source.

evidence.supports: The 4th Dynasty settlement we discovered here proved to be an urban settlement that sprawled across more than 7 hectares

date.label: Old Kingdom (2575-2134 BC)
date.basis: As the cited source gives it.

events.statement: The excavators infer from the volume of the bread moulds found at Giza that the bread baked in them was leavened; the date is that of the bakeries in the first event, not stated in this sentence.

evidence.supports: The volume of our bread molds indicates that bread cooked in them must have been leavened.

earliest_record.rationale: The earliest dated evidence found for this capability in this community. No review has yet confirmed that nothing earlier exists.

unresolved.note: Direct evidence of leavening at Giza (yeast or sourdough residues); the leavening here is the excavators' inference from mould volume, and Samuel 1996 on yeast in Egyptian loaves was not reached.
The years of the bakeries: the sources give the 4th Dynasty and the Old Kingdom span 2575-2134 BC; narrowing to the reigns of Khafre and Menkaure needs a source that states the years.
Whether Mesopotamian leavened bread came earlier and whether Egyptian leavening was independent.
Whether Greek and Roman leavened bread descended from Egyptian practice.

research.note: The sources describe Old Kingdom bakeries and infer leavening; they do not say whether leavening was first achieved in Egypt or reached separately from Mesopotamia.
